The Pittsburgh Press
Sunday, April 5, 1987
TRAVEL Non-smoking passengers win more than they lose in airplane roulette
Observations and cogitations by this and other travelers ... Apparently every seat on a Flori- da-bound plane had been sold, and stand-bys were standing by fever "notice that stand-bys seldom sit?) "Because of the crowd today," said the airline agent making seat 'assignments, "I'm going to make the whoje plane non-smoking."
: Probably he was just trying to fill every seat, but applause broke out among the waiting passengers .. - How quickly some things change. Not very long ago, many considered cigarette smoking smart, something done with flair in the movies. Now smoking has come to be perceived as a public nuisance.
-A smoking friend says he is begin- ning to feel like a social outcast. Another friend, with whom I was lunching, leaned below the table to avold detection as she lit & cigaret(6
Gilbert Love
